title: How many barrels of crude oil will the Strategic Petroleum Reserve hold on the following dates?
short_title: What will the strategic petroleum reserve levels be in these months?
url_title: What will the strategic petroleum reserve levels be in these months?

group_of_questions.description:
The United States of America started in the 1970s to main an emergency stockpile of oil called the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR). The SPR is under command of the President (and Congress), who can initiate sale of this oil in cases where this is deemed fit (such as domestic shortages, natural disasters, and wars). The main goal of the SPR is to [“alleviate significant oil supply disruptions or price inflation”](https://www.cfr.org/backgrounder/how-does-us-government-use-strategic-petroleum-reserve#:~:text=The%20SPR%20is%20the%20world's,supply%20disruptions%20or%20price%20inflation.) primarily domestically but also internationally. Most recently, the SPR has been tapped during the COVID-19 pandemic and in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, according to the [CFR](https://www.cfr.org/backgrounder/how-does-us-government-use-strategic-petroleum-reserve#:~:text=The%20SPR%20is%20the%20world's,supply%20disruptions%20or%20price%20inflation.):

> The most recent releases before the war were due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent rebound in oil demand, as rising gasoline prices contributed to record inflation in the United States. In November 2021, President Biden announced a release of thirty-two million barrels in exchange agreements and eighteen million barrels in sales, seen as an effort to pressure OPEC to increase production; some experts said it was a novel use of the SPR, given there was no supply disruption.

> In March 2022, as Russia’s war in Ukraine caused turmoil in global energy markets, Biden authorized an emergency release of thirty million barrels, as part of a coordinated action led by the IEA. Later that month, he approved the emergency release of up to one million barrels per day for six months, or a total of about 180 million barrels—the largest release in the reserve’s history. Biden said the move was a “wartime bridge” that would allow domestic oil production time to ramp up. By October of that year, the Department of Energy had completed its emergency sale from the stockpile, bringing the reserve down to fewer than four hundred million barrels, a four-decade low. The administration said it will use the revenue to replenish the reserve by purchasing oil when the price of West Texas Intermediate (a U.S. benchmark) is \$72 per barrel or less.

The size of the SPR (in barrels of crude oil) is tracked by the [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET\&s=MCSSTUS1\&f=M). Below the number of crude oil barrels (in thousands) of the SPR.

| Mar-2021 | 637,774                       |

| Dec-2021 | 593,682                       |

In [January 2023](https://www.cnbc.com/2023/01/27/house-republicans-pass-bill-to-limit-strategic-petroleum-reserve-draws.html), the US House of Representative passed a bill that aims at reducing the president’s authority to draw down the SPR for a reason other than “severe energy supply disruption”.

> Despite passing the House, the legislation is all but certain never to be signed into law. It lacks the support to pass the Democratic-controlled Senate and the White House has said Biden will veto it if it ever comes to his desk.

In [February 2023](https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/biden-sell-26-million-barrels-more-strategic-petroleum-reserve), the Biden administration announced plans for further sales (of 26 million barrels between April 1 and June 30, which is expected to bring the SPR to the lowest levels since 1983.

group_of_questions.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the number of barrels of crude oil that are held in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve for the respective month. This will resolve based on the [EIA monthly data -  MCSSTUS1](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET\&s=MCSSTUS1\&f=M). For example, the number for September 2022 was 416,393 thousand barrels, which would resolve as 416,393,000.

If the EIA stops updating this tracker, the question will resolve as ambiguous
